arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Allyson Ho argued that courts have adjudicated patent disputes for four hundred years.
Ho claimed Congress improperly transferred this judicial power to an executive tribunal.
Ho stated that the Patent Trial and Appeal Board has five unusual features.
Justice Ginsburg questioned whether the Patent Office can correct its own errors under Article III.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether Congress can assign patent cancellation to executive branch judges. Oil States claims this power belongs to Article III courts. Greene's Energy argues the board acts as a valid public rights tribunal.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Oil States wants the Supreme Court to strike down the inter partes review process.
Greene's Energy wants the Supreme Court to uphold the board's authority to cancel patents.

Greene's Energy argues that patent validity is a public right that executive judges can review.
